# Inflation Risk with Fixed-Rate CDs

When you earn a fixed rate of interest on a CD, inflation is a risk because **inflation can grow faster than your money, lowering your real returns over time**.

In other words, if inflation rises at a higher rate than the interest your CD is earning, the purchasing power of your money decreases. Your money grows in nominal terms, but its actual value and what it can buy may not keep pace with rising prices in the economy.

Even though your CD pays a guaranteed fixed rate, inflation can rise faster than that rate. This means the purchasing power of your money—including the interest earned—can actually decrease over time, effectively lowering your real return, even though the dollar amount you receive is guaranteed.
